Add ps.isolated: run Python code inside another Python environment (#12)

* Add ps.isolated: run Python code inside another Python environment

One stdlib-only module merging the copies of this mechanism in arioso
(_isolated), voxy (envs, worker, workers/serve.py) and foley (the one-shot
runner of its stable_audio_3 source):

- Runtime: where a hand-installed environment lives ($<env_var>, else
  $<base_dir_var>/<name>, else <default_dir>/<name>); RuntimeNotInstalled
  carries the install commands.
- EnvSpec + ensure_env/is_env_ready/env_commands: uv-built environments
  with a digest marker (a changed spec rebuilds; host UV_CONSTRAINT cleared).
- Worker: a long-lived JSON-lines process; module drivers (python -m, with
  expose= for the packages it may import) or adapter files (loaded by this
  module standalone, so the environment needs no ps). stderr to a log whose
  tail goes into errors; failed load stops it; an interrupted or garbled
  exchange kills it; host PYTHONPATH/PYTHONHOME/VIRTUAL_ENV never passed.
- WorkerPool, serve, serve_adapter, adapter_handler, run_process,
  venv_python (POSIX or Windows layout), clean_environ.

Refs thorwhalen/arioso#56

* Doctest: match ls's help case-insensitively (uutils coreutils on ubuntu-26.04 capitalises it)

* ps.isolated: adapter files only, smaller surface, review fixes

Decisions (review of this PR): one driver style, adapter files; WorkerPool
stays with its one customer (voxy); no build=False / env_commands / uv= /
adapter_handler / serve(handle) / expose.

Fixes:
- Worker.kill() takes no lock and is what runs at exit, so a host exits
  even with a daemon thread inside call(); tested with a real host process.
- A stale environment is removed and rebuilt (a changed Python or a dropped
  requirement takes effect); a folder that is not a venv is never removed.
- stderr= seam: a log file (default: temporary, made on start, deleted on
  close) or None for the host's terminal; the log tail is read by seeking.
- serve_adapter puts the adapter's folder on sys.path (shared helpers).
- run_process kills the whole process tree on timeout (ps.util gains
  kill_process_tree and NEW_PROCESS_GROUP); still raises TimeoutExpired.
- UV_OVERRIDE and UV_BUILD_CONSTRAINT are cleared with UV_CONSTRAINT, and the
  build notice shows the commands with them cleared.
- Only None results become {}.
- ps/__init__ resolves commands lazily (PEP 562): import ps and its
  submodules no longer scan PATH; ps.<cmd>, from ps import <cmd> and dir(ps)
  still work.

Refs thorwhalen/arioso#56

* tests: Windows-safe fake install names; log tail may end in CRLF

* ps.isolated: only rebuild environments ps built; workers lead their own process group

- ensure_env deletes a stale environment only when it holds ps's marker
  (a provisional one is written right after `uv venv`, so a half-built env
  still counts as ps's); a non-empty folder without it raises, and the
  running interpreter's own environment is never replaced.
- Workers start in their own process group; stopping one kills what it
  spawned (a forked data loader), and kill() closes stdin only, so exit no
  longer waits on a child holding the reply pipe.
- kill_process_tree kills the POSIX group even when the leader already
  exited; documents what Windows taskkill /T cannot reach.
- ps/__init__: lazy __all__ for `from ps import *`, a locked first scan,
  submodule guard from pkgutil; README notes the __dict__ change.
- Docs: exit-time kill only helps daemon threads; process-group children
  leave the terminal's group.
